lessons.title: Column, bar, line and pie charts
learn: Insert, switch row and column, select data
lessons.mac:
Insert tab chart buttons are icons: hover to see Column, Line, Pie
Or use Insert > Recommended Charts
Chart Design and Format tabs appear only when a chart is selected
Undo: ⌘ Z

steps.say: Here's where we're heading: a column chart comparing four regions month by month, a line chart for the North trend, and a pie chart of each region's share of the year. These three cover most charts in a monthly review.

acts.h: Go to the sheet S11-02 Done

steps.say: In this lesson you'll insert column, line and pie charts, switch rows and columns, and add titles and labels. Open the sheet called S11-02 to follow along.

acts.t:
In this lesson
• Insert column, line and pie charts
• Switch row and column, pick the right data
• Add a title and data labels
Practice sheet: S11-02

steps.say: Choose the chart by the question. Columns and bars compare amounts, a line shows a trend over time, and a pie shows share of a whole when you have five slices or fewer. Always select the data with its headers first, then insert.

acts.t:
Pick the chart by the question
Column or bar: compare amounts across categories
Line: show a trend over time
Pie: share of a whole, five slices or fewer
Rule: select the data with headers, then insert

steps.say: Our data has months in column A and four regions across. Select A1 to E13. I'm leaving out the Total row in row fourteen on purpose, and you'll see why in a minute.
Go to the Insert tab, click Column and pick Clustered Column. Excel puts the months on the axis and draws four bars per month, one for each region.

To compare regions side by side instead, click Switch Row slash Column on the Chart Design tab. Now the regions sit on the axis and each month is a series. Twelve colours is too busy, so click it again to switch back.
Click the placeholder that says Chart Title and type a title that tells the story: Monthly sales by region, FY 2025-26. Press Return to confirm.

acts.h: Type Monthly sales by region, FY 2025-26 and press Return

steps.say: Now a very common mistake. Select A1 to E14, which includes the Total row, and insert another clustered column chart.
The Total bars tower over everything and squash the monthly bars flat. Press Command Z to undo. The rule is simple: never chart a total together with its parts.
For a trend, select A1 to B13, just the months and the North column. On the Insert tab click Line and choose Line. One series, twelve points, and the dips are easy to spot.
The FY totals in G1 to H5 add up to the full year, so they suit a pie. Select them, click Pie on the Insert tab and pick Pie. Four slices, one per region.
Readers want the percentage on each slice, not a legend to decode. On Chart Design, open Quick Layout and choose Layout 1. It writes each region's name and percentage on its slice.
Charts stay linked to their cells. In B2, type thirty-five lakh and press Return. The April bar, the North line and the pie all update together.
Press Command Z to put the original April figure back.
On Excel for Mac, the chart buttons on the Insert tab are icons, so hover to read their names, or use Recommended Charts. The Chart Design and Format tabs only appear while a chart is selected.

acts.t:
Mac corner
Insert tab chart buttons are icons: hover to see Column, Line, Pie
Or use Insert > Recommended Charts
Chart Design and Format tabs appear only when a chart is selected
Undo: ⌘ Z

steps.say: To recap: select the data with headers and leave totals out, match the chart to the question, and use Switch Row slash Column to change what sits on the axis.

acts.t:
Recap
• Select data with headers, leave totals out
• Column compares, line trends, pie shows share
• Switch Row/Column changes what goes on the axis

steps.say: Your challenge: make a clustered bar chart of the FY totals in G1 to H5 and give it a title that names the top region. The answer is on the S11-02 Done sheet.

acts.t:
Challenge
Insert a clustered bar chart of G1:H5
Give it a title that names the top region
Answer: sheet S11-02 Done

lessons.title: Formatting charts that read clearly
lessons.mac:
⌘ 1 opens the Format pane for the selected element
Format tab > Chart Elements box picks any element
Templates (.crtx) save on Excel for Mac, not in Excel for the web

steps.say: This is plain sales data turned into a chart your manager reads in two seconds. The bars are sorted, the clutter is gone, and one product stands out in orange. Change one cell and the highlight moves.

acts.h: Go to the sheet S11-03 Done

steps.say: You'll sort the data, highlight one bar with a helper column, strip the clutter, and save the look as a template. We're recording in Excel desktop; the menus match Excel for Mac. Practice sheet S11-03.

acts.t:
In this lesson
• Sort the data and remove clutter
• Highlight one bar with a helper column
• Save the look as a chart template
Practice sheet: S11-03

steps.say: Here's the idea. A helper column repeats the sales only for the product named in F1 and returns hash N A for the rest. Charts don't draw hash N A, so the helper draws just one bar, which we lay on top of the original.

acts.t:
Highlight with a helper column
=IF(A2=$F$1, B2, NA())
Matching product: shows its sales
Every other product: #N/A, which a chart skips
Then set Series Overlap to 100%

steps.say: First, sort. Select A1 to B9, then on the Data tab click Sort. Sort by Sales, order Largest to Smallest, and click OK. A sorted chart reads like a ranking.
In C2, type equals IF, open bracket, then the test: A2 equals dollar F dollar 1, comma. F1 holds the product to highlight, and the dollars lock it for every row.
If it matches, return B2, the sales, then a comma.
Otherwise return NA, open and close bracket. Close the IF bracket and press Return.
Select C2 to C9 and press Command D to fill down. Only Sunflower Oil shows a number. Every other row shows hash N A, which is exactly what we want.

acts.h: Select C2:C9 and fill down with ⌘ + D

steps.say: Select A1 to C9. On the Insert tab click Recommended Charts, go to All Charts, choose Bar and click OK.
Look at the chart. The orange bar sits beside a blue one instead of on top of it, and the biggest product is at the bottom. Both are default settings, and both are quick to fix.

On the Format tab, open the selection box on the left and pick Series Highlight, then click Format Selection. On a Mac, Command 1 opens the same pane. Set Series Overlap to one hundred percent and Gap Width to sixty.
Open the same selection box, pick Vertical Category Axis and click Format Selection. Tick Categories in reverse order. The biggest product moves to the top, just like the sorted table.
Now remove clutter. On Chart Design, click Add Chart Element, Gridlines, and switch off Primary Major Vertical. Then Add Chart Element, Legend, None.
Add data labels at Outside End so nobody needs the value axis. Then Add Chart Element, Axes, and switch off Primary Horizontal, because the labels do its job now.
Click Chart Title and type a title that states the message: Sunflower Oil 1L, our number 2 product, FY 2025-26. Press Return.

acts.h: Type Sunflower Oil 1L: our number 2 product, FY 2025-26 and press Return

steps.say: Here's the payoff. In F1, type Ghee 1L and press Return. The orange highlight jumps to Ghee, so in a review you can spotlight any product in seconds.
To reuse this design, right-click the chart and choose Save as Template. Next time pick it from All Charts, Templates. On a Mac, Control-click the chart for the same menu.

acts.t:
Save the look as a template
Right-click the chart > Save as Template > name it 'Highlight bar'
Reuse: Insert > Recommended Charts > All Charts > Templates
Mac: Control-click the chart > Save as Template

steps.say: On Excel for Mac, Command 1 opens the Format pane for whatever is selected, and the Format tab has the same Chart Elements box. Excel for the web can't save chart templates, so do that step on your Mac.

acts.t:
Mac corner
⌘ 1 opens the Format pane for the selected element
Format tab > Chart Elements box picks any element
Templates (.crtx) save on Excel for Mac, not in Excel for the web

steps.say: To recap: sort before you chart, use a helper column with NA to highlight one bar, and remove anything that doesn't help the message.

acts.t:
Recap
• Sort the data so the chart reads like a ranking
• Helper column + NA() + Overlap 100% = highlight
• Remove gridlines, legend and axes the labels replace

steps.say: Your challenge: replace the typed name in F1 with a formula that always picks the top seller, so the highlight updates itself. The answer is on S11-03 Done.

acts.t:
Challenge
Put a formula in F1 that returns the product with the highest sales
Hint: INDEX and MATCH with MAX
Answer: sheet S11-03 Done

lessons.title: Combo charts and a secondary axis
learn: Target line on a column chart
lessons.mac:
Select separate ranges: hold ⌘ while dragging
Fill a selection with one entry: ⌃ Return
Chart Design > Change Chart Type > Combo

steps.say: Here's a chart finance teams love: monthly sales as columns, with gross margin percent as a line on its own scale on the right. Below it, sales against a flat target line. Two very different numbers, one clear picture.

acts.h: Go to the sheet S11-04 Done

steps.say: You'll calculate margin, build a combo chart with a secondary axis, and add a target line. Practice sheet S11-04, recorded in Excel desktop with the same menus as Excel for Mac.

acts.t:
In this lesson
• Calculate margin %
• Combo chart: columns + line on a secondary axis
• Add a target line
Practice sheet: S11-04

steps.say: A combo chart mixes two chart types. Columns show rupee amounts on the left axis. A line shows a percentage or a target. Use a secondary axis only when the line's numbers are on a completely different scale.

acts.t:
Combo chart = two chart types in one
Columns: amounts in ₹ (left axis)
Line: a % or a target
Secondary axis: a second scale, only for different units

steps.say: First we need the margin. In D2, type equals C2 divided by B2 and press Return. Gross profit divided by sales; the column is already formatted as a percentage.
Select D2 to D13 and press Command D to fill down. April's margin is about 23 percent.

acts.h: Select D2:D13 and fill down with ⌘ + D

steps.say: We want months, sales and margin, but not gross profit. In the Name Box I type A1 to B13, a comma, then D1 to D13. With a mouse, hold Command while you drag the second range.
Now the common mistake. Insert a plain clustered column chart: Recommended Charts, All Charts, Column, OK.
The margin bars are invisible. Margins are less than one, and the axis runs to lakhs of rupees, so they sit flat on the floor. One axis can't serve both.
Fix it with Change Chart Type on the Chart Design tab. Choose Combo, set Margin percent to Line with Markers, tick its Secondary Axis box and click OK. The line now has its own scale on the right.
Label the new axis. Add Chart Element, Axis Titles, Secondary Vertical. Click the new Axis Title, type Margin percent and press Return.
Click Chart Title, type Sales and margin percent, FY 2025-26, and press Return.

acts.h: Type Sales and margin %, FY 2025-26 and press Return

steps.say: Now a target line. Select A1 to B13 and E1 to E13, then Insert, Recommended Charts, All Charts, Combo.
Set Target to Line and leave Secondary Axis unticked. Target and sales are both rupees, so they share one axis. Put a target on a secondary axis and it floats at the wrong height. Click OK.
Targets change mid-year. Select E2 to E13, type twenty-eight lakh, and press Control Return to fill every selected cell at once. The line jumps up and you see straight away which months fall short.
On Excel for Mac, hold Command to select separate ranges, and Control Return fills a selection with one entry. Change Chart Type sits on the Chart Design tab, exactly as here.

acts.t:
Mac corner
Select separate ranges: hold ⌘ while dragging
Fill a selection with one entry: ⌃ Return
Chart Design > Change Chart Type > Combo

steps.say: To recap: combo charts mix columns and lines, a secondary axis is only for different units, and a target in rupees shares the main axis.

acts.t:
Recap
• Combo = columns for amounts + line for % or target
• Secondary axis only for different units
• Targets share the rupee axis

steps.say: Your challenge: in G1, count how many months are below the target in E2, using COUNTIF. The answer is on S11-04 Done.

acts.t:
Challenge
In G1, count the months where sales are below the target in E2
Hint: COUNTIF with "<"&E2
Answer: sheet S11-04 Done

lessons.title: Waterfall chart for a profit bridge
lessons.mac:
Insert > Waterfall button (or Insert > Recommended Charts > All Charts)
Select one bar: click, pause, click again
Command 1 > Series Options > Set as total

steps.say: By the end of this lesson you'll have a profit bridge: revenue of four hundred eighty-five lakh rupees stepping down through every cost to a net profit of sixty-four lakh. Finance heads use this chart to explain where the money went.

acts.t:
What we'll build
A waterfall chart of Shree Ganesh Foods, FY 2025-26 (₹ lakh)
Revenue 485 steps down through costs to Net profit 64
Gross profit, EBITDA and Net profit stand on the axis as totals

steps.say: You'll write the subtotal formulas, insert a waterfall, and set the totals. Practice sheet S11-05, recorded in Excel desktop; I'll show the Mac menu at the end.

acts.t:
In this lesson
• Subtotal formulas for the bridge
• Insert a waterfall chart
• Set subtotals as totals
Practice sheet: S11-05

steps.say: In a waterfall, positive numbers step up and negative numbers step down. Subtotals must be marked Set as total, or Excel treats them as one more increase. So costs go in as negative numbers.

acts.t:
Waterfall chart
Positive = step up, negative = step down
Subtotals: Set as total so they start from zero
Enter costs as negative numbers

steps.say: The yellow cells need formulas. In B4, type equals SUM, open bracket, B2 colon B3, close bracket, and press Return. Revenue plus a negative cost gives gross profit of two hundred twenty-four lakh.
In B9, EBITDA is gross profit less the operating costs: equals SUM of B4 to B8. That's one hundred eight point five lakh.
In B13, net profit: equals SUM of B9 to B12. Sixty-four lakh.
Select A1 to B13. On the Insert tab click Recommended Charts, then All Charts, Waterfall, and OK.
Look at Gross profit. It floats in mid-air as if it were another increase, and so do EBITDA and Net profit. Excel can't tell a subtotal from an ordinary number, so we tell it.

Select just the Gross profit bar. With a mouse you click the bar, pause, and click it again. Here I pick it from the selection box on the Format tab, click Format Selection, and tick Set as total. It drops to the axis.
Do the same for EBITDA.
And for Net profit. Now the three totals stand on the axis, and every cost hangs between them.
Click Chart Title, type Profit bridge FY 2025-26, rupees in lakh, and press Return.

acts.h: Type Profit bridge FY 2025-26 (₹ lakh) and press Return

steps.say: Another classic mistake is typing a cost as a positive number. Change B3 to two hundred sixty-one. The cost bar now goes up, and every total below it is wrong.
Press Command Z to undo. Costs always go in with a minus sign.
Now prove it's live. Change revenue in B2 to five hundred ten. Every subtotal recalculates and the bridge redraws. Net profit is now eighty-nine lakh.
On a Mac, use Insert, then the waterfall chart button, or Recommended Charts. Click a bar twice to select it, and press Command 1 for the Format pane with Set as total.

acts.t:
Mac corner
Insert > Waterfall button (or Insert > Recommended Charts > All Charts)
Select one bar: click, pause, click again
Command 1 > Series Options > Set as total

steps.say: To recap: costs are negative, subtotals are formulas, and each subtotal bar must be set as a total.

acts.t:
Recap
• Enter costs as negative numbers
• Subtotals are SUM formulas
• Mark each subtotal: Set as total

steps.say: Your challenge: make tax a formula, twenty-five point one seven percent of profit before tax, rounded to two decimals. The answer is on S11-05 Done.

acts.t:
Challenge
In B12, replace -21.5 with a formula: 25.17% of (B9+B10+B11), negative, rounded to 2 decimals
Answer: sheet S11-05 Done

lessons.title: Histogram, Pareto and box-and-whisker
lessons.mac:
Insert > Statistic Chart button > Histogram, Pareto, Box and Whisker
Or Insert > Recommended Charts > All Charts
Bin width: select the axis, ⌘ 1

steps.say: Three charts about how numbers are spread out: a histogram of sixty order values, a Pareto chart that shows which complaints cause most of the pain, and a box plot comparing regions. They answer questions averages hide.

acts.t:
What we'll build
Histogram: 60 order values in ₹5,000 bins
Pareto: the few complaint types behind most complaints
Box and whisker: order values by region
Practice sheet: S11-06

steps.say: You'll check the median and quartiles with formulas, then build each chart and read it. We're in Excel desktop; the Mac menus are at the end.

acts.t:
In this lesson
• MEDIAN and QUARTILE.INC as a check
• Histogram with clean bins
• Pareto and box-and-whisker

steps.say: A histogram counts how many values fall in each range, called a bin. A Pareto sorts categories largest first and adds a cumulative percentage line. A box plot shows the median, the middle half, and unusual values.

acts.t:
Histogram: count of values in each bin
Pareto: bars largest first + cumulative % line
Box and whisker: line = median, box = middle 50%, whiskers = the rest, dots = outliers

steps.say: First, numbers to check the charts against. In I3, type equals MEDIAN of C2 to C61 and press Return. Half the orders are below about ten thousand rupees.
In I4, type equals QUARTILE dot INC, open bracket, C2 colon C61, comma 1, close bracket. A quarter of orders are below this value.
In I5, the same formula with 3 gives the third quartile. The middle half of all orders sits between I4 and I5.
Select C1 to C61, the order values with the header. Insert, Recommended Charts, All Charts, Histogram, OK.
Excel's automatic bins have awkward edges. On the Format tab, pick Horizontal Category Axis and click Format Selection. Set Bin width to five thousand, then tick Overflow bin at thirty thousand.
Click Chart Title and type Order values, FY 2025-26. Most orders fall in the first few bins, with a thin tail of large orders.

acts.h: Type Order values, FY 2025-26 and press Return

steps.say: Now the complaints. Select E1 to F9. Insert, Recommended Charts, All Charts, Histogram, then choose the Pareto option and click OK. Excel sorts the bars for you and adds the cumulative line.
Read the line on the right axis. Late delivery, refund delay and wrong item together make up about three quarters of all complaints. Fix those three first.
For the box plot, a common mistake is selecting only the values. Select C1 to C61 and insert a Box and Whisker chart. You get one box for the whole company, which hides the regional story.
Press Command Z. Select B1 to C61 this time, region and value together, and insert the Box and Whisker again. Now there's one box per region.
In each box, the line is the median, the box holds the middle half of orders, and the dots are unusually large orders worth a closer look. Compare the overall median in I3 with each region's line.
One big order shows why the median is useful. In C2, type ninety-five thousand. The histogram's overflow bar and a new dot appear, while the median in I3 barely moves. Press Command Z to undo.
On Excel for Mac, these three live under the Insert tab's statistic chart button, or Recommended Charts, All Charts. Command 1 opens the Format pane for bins.

acts.t:
Mac corner
Insert > Statistic Chart button > Histogram, Pareto, Box and Whisker
Or Insert > Recommended Charts > All Charts
Bin width: select the axis, ⌘ 1

steps.say: To recap: histograms show spread, Pareto finds the vital few, and box plots compare groups.

acts.t:
Recap
• Histogram: set a sensible bin width
• Pareto: sorted bars + cumulative %
• Box plot: select the group column too

steps.say: Your challenge: in I7, count the orders above twenty thousand rupees with COUNTIF. Check that the number matches the tall end of your histogram. The answer is on S11-06 Done.

acts.t:
Challenge
In I7, count orders above ₹20,000 with COUNTIF
Compare with the histogram's right-hand bars
Answer: sheet S11-06 Done

lessons.title: Treemap, sunburst and funnel
lessons.mac:
Insert > Hierarchy Chart button > Treemap, Sunburst
Insert > Waterfall button > Funnel
Or Insert > Recommended Charts > All Charts

steps.say: In this lesson you'll build three shape charts: a treemap and a sunburst showing which categories drive sales, and a funnel showing how forty-eight thousand website visits shrink to two hundred forty-five deals.

acts.t:
What we'll build
Treemap: category and sub-category share of sales
Sunburst: the same data as rings
Funnel: 48,000 visits down to 245 deals won
Practice sheet: S11-07

steps.say: You'll lay out hierarchy data correctly, insert all three charts, and add conversion percentages beside the funnel. Recorded in Excel desktop; Mac menus at the end.

acts.t:
In this lesson
• Hierarchy data layout
• Treemap and sunburst
• Funnel with conversion %

steps.say: Treemaps size rectangles by value and group them by category. Sunbursts show the same as rings. Funnels show stages that shrink. For hierarchy charts, the parent column comes first, the child next, the value last.

acts.t:
Treemap: rectangles sized by value, grouped by category
Sunburst: inner ring = category, outer = sub-category
Funnel: stages from largest to smallest
Layout: parent, child, value; keep each parent's rows together

steps.say: Look at A1 to C12. Category in column A, sub-category in B, sales in C, and all rows for one category sit together. Select A1 to C12.
Insert, Recommended Charts, All Charts, Treemap, OK. Electronics takes the biggest block, nearly half of all sales.
Click Chart Title and type Sales by category, FY 2025-26.

acts.h: Type Sales by category, FY 2025-26 and press Return

steps.say: Select A1 to C12 again and insert a Sunburst from All Charts. Categories form the inner ring and sub-categories the outer ring. It's handy when you have three levels.
Now the funnel. First the conversion rates. In G3, type equals F3 divided by F2 and press Return. Twenty percent of visits became leads.
Select G3 to G6 and press Command D. Each cell divides a stage by the stage before it.

acts.h: Select G3:G6 and fill down with ⌘ + D

steps.say: Here's the common mistake. Select E1 to G6, including the percentage column, and insert a Funnel. Excel adds the percentages as a second series of tiny bars that make no sense.
Press Command Z. Select just E1 to F6, stage and count, and insert the Funnel again. Clean bars, largest at the top, with data labels.
Click Chart Title and type Sales funnel, Q2 FY 2025-26, and press Return.

acts.h: Type Sales funnel, Q2 FY 2025-26 and press Return

steps.say: Change Deals won in F6 to three hundred. The last bar grows and G6 shows the proposal win rate rising to almost thirty-five percent.
On Excel for Mac, treemap and sunburst sit under the Insert tab's hierarchy chart button, and funnel under the waterfall button. Recommended Charts, All Charts works too.

acts.t:
Mac corner
Insert > Hierarchy Chart button > Treemap, Sunburst
Insert > Waterfall button > Funnel
Or Insert > Recommended Charts > All Charts

steps.say: To recap: hierarchy data goes parent, child, value; treemaps and sunbursts show share; funnels show drop-off stage by stage.

acts.t:
Recap
• Hierarchy layout: parent, child, value
• Treemap and sunburst show share
• Funnel: select only stage and count

steps.say: Your challenge: in H2, work out the overall conversion from website visits to deals won, as a percentage with two decimals. The answer is on S11-07 Done.

acts.t:
Challenge
In H2, calculate deals won ÷ website visits
Format as 0.00%
Answer: sheet S11-07 Done

lessons.title: Map chart of Indian states
lessons.mac:
Insert > Maps > Filled Map
Needs Microsoft 365 and internet
Series options: select the map, ⌘ 1

steps.say: We'll build a filled map of India with each state shaded by sales, darker for higher sales. It's the fastest way to show a national sales head where the business is strong and where it's thin.

acts.t:
What we'll build
A filled map of India: 20 states shaded by FY 2025-26 sales
Two state names Excel can't place, fixed
Map zoomed to India with labels
Practice sheet: S11-08

steps.say: You'll set up the data so Excel finds every state, insert the map, fix the names it can't place, and zoom it to India. Recorded in Excel desktop; it needs an internet connection.

acts.t:
In this lesson
• Data layout for map charts
• Insert a filled map
• Fix locations Excel can't find

steps.say: A map chart needs one column of places and one of values. Add a Country column with India, so Excel doesn't confuse Punjab or Hyderabad with places in other countries. Use official state names.

acts.t:
Filled map chart
One column of places + one column of values
Add Country = India to avoid wrong matches
Uses Bing to find places: needs internet
Official state names match best

steps.say: Our sheet has Country in column A, State in B and Sales in C, for twenty states. Select A1 to C21.
Insert, Recommended Charts, All Charts, Map, and OK. Excel sends the place names to Bing and shades each state.

Look at the east and the far north. Odisha and Jammu and Kashmir aren't shaded properly, because our data says Orissa and J and K: an old name and a short form. This is the most common map chart problem.
Fix the source data. In B15, type Odisha and press Return.
In B19, type Jammu and Kashmir and press Return. The map refreshes and both regions are shaded.

acts.h: Type Jammu and Kashmir and press Return

steps.say: Now zoom to India. On the Format tab pick Series Sales and click Format Selection. Set Map area to Only regions with data, and Map labels to Show all.

acts.h: Set Map area to Only regions with data

steps.say: Click Chart Title and type Sales by state, FY 2025-26.

acts.h: Type Sales by state, FY 2025-26 and press Return

steps.say: The map is live. Change Kerala's sales in C11 to two crore ten lakh. Kerala turns darker straight away.
On Excel for Mac, go to Insert, Maps, Filled Map. It needs Microsoft 365 and an internet connection, and Command 1 opens the same series options.

acts.t:
Mac corner
Insert > Maps > Filled Map
Needs Microsoft 365 and internet
Series options: select the map, ⌘ 1

steps.say: To recap: add a Country column, use official names, and zoom the map to regions with data.

acts.t:
Recap
• Country column + one place column + values
• Fix names Excel can't place in the data
• Map area: Only regions with data

steps.say: Your challenge: add Chhattisgarh with sales of thirty-four lakh in row 22, then extend the chart's data range with Select Data. The answer is on S11-08 Done.

acts.t:
Challenge
Row 22: India, Chhattisgarh, 3400000
Chart Design > Select Data > A1:C22
Answer: sheet S11-08 Done

lessons.title: Sparklines
lessons.mac:
Insert > Sparklines > Line, Column or Win/Loss
Sparkline tab appears when a sparkline cell is selected
Axis > Same for All Sparklines for fair comparison

steps.say: We'll put a tiny trend line inside a cell for each of eight branches, mark the best and worst months, and add win-loss bars that show which months beat target. A whole year per branch in one glance.

acts.t:
What we'll build
Line sparklines for 8 branches with high and low points
Win/Loss sparklines: months above or below target
A 'Best month' formula beside them
Practice sheet: S11-09

steps.say: You'll insert line and win-loss sparklines, mark points, put them on a common scale, and find each branch's best month. Recorded in Excel desktop; the Mac menus are the same.

acts.t:
In this lesson
• Line and Win/Loss sparklines
• High, low and negative points
• Same axis for every sparkline

steps.say: Sparklines are tiny charts inside a single cell. Line shows a trend, Column shows each month's size, and Win/Loss shows only whether a value is above or below zero. You pick a data range and a location range.

acts.t:
Sparklines: a tiny chart in one cell
Line = trend · Column = size · Win/Loss = above or below zero
Insert > Sparklines > choose Data Range and Location Range
Remove with Sparkline > Clear

steps.say: Rows 2 to 9 hold monthly sales in lakh for each branch, April to March. Select N2 to N9, where the sparklines will go.
On the Insert tab, in the Sparklines group, click Line. For Data Range type B2 colon M9, then click OK.
On the Sparkline tab, tick High Point and Low Point. Each line now marks its best and worst month.
Here's the common mistake. Each sparkline has its own scale, so a small branch looks as dramatic as a big one. Kolkata's line swings as much as Mumbai's even though the numbers are very different.
Fix it under Axis on the Sparkline tab. Choose Same for All Sparklines for the vertical axis minimum, then open Axis again and choose it for the maximum. Now every line shares one scale.
Rows 12 to 19 show sales minus target. Select N12 to N19, click Win/Loss on the Insert tab, type B12 colon M19 as the Data Range, and click OK.
Tick Negative Points on the Sparkline tab. Missed months turn red, and patterns jump out, like a branch that misses three months running.
Now name the best month. In O2, type equals INDEX, open bracket, dollar B dollar 1 colon dollar M dollar 1, comma. That's the row of month names, locked.
Then MATCH, open bracket, MAX of B2 to M2, comma, B2 to M2, comma, zero, and close both brackets. MATCH finds where the highest sale sits. Press Return.
Select O2 to O9 and press Command D. Each branch shows the month of its peak, matching the high point marker.

acts.h: Select O2:O9 and fill down with ⌘ + D

steps.say: Change Pune's April sales in B3 to sixty lakh. The sparkline spikes at the start, the high point moves, and O3 now says April.
On Excel for Mac, it's Insert, Sparklines, then Line, Column or Win/Loss. The Sparkline tab appears when you select a sparkline cell.

acts.t:
Mac corner
Insert > Sparklines > Line, Column or Win/Loss
Sparkline tab appears when a sparkline cell is selected
Axis > Same for All Sparklines for fair comparison

steps.say: To recap: sparklines live inside cells, mark high and low points, and use the same axis when comparing rows.

acts.t:
Recap
• Insert > Sparklines: data range + location
• Mark High, Low and Negative points
• Same for All Sparklines for fair comparison

steps.say: Your challenge: change the line sparklines in N2 to N9 into column sparklines and mark the last point. The answer is on S11-09 Done.

Tick Last Point
Answer: sheet S11-09 Done

lessons.title: Dynamic charts
learn: Charts from Tables grow with data
lessons.mac:
⌘ T creates a Table
Data > Data Validation > List
Link a title: select it, type = in the formula bar, click the cell

steps.say: Two charts that keep themselves up to date. The line chart grows when you add a month, and the column chart switches region when you pick from a dropdown, with a title that changes too.

acts.h: Go to the sheet S11-10 Done

steps.say: You'll build a chart on a Table, a dropdown with INDEX and MATCH helper cells, and a chart title linked to a cell. Practice sheet S11-10, recorded in Excel desktop.

acts.t:
In this lesson
• Charts from Tables grow with data
• Dropdown-driven chart with INDEX and MATCH
• A chart title linked to a cell

steps.say: There are two ways to make a chart dynamic. Build it on a Table, so new rows join the chart. Or build it on helper cells that a dropdown controls.

acts.t:
Two ways to make a chart dynamic
1) Build it on a Table (⌘ T): new rows join the chart
2) Helper cells: INDEX(row, MATCH(choice, headers, 0))
Link the title: select it, type =, pick the cell

steps.say: Click A1 and press Command T. Check that My table has headers is ticked and click OK. Our April to February sales are now a Table.
Select A1 to B12 and insert a line chart: Recommended Charts, All Charts, Line, OK.
Now March arrives. In A13 type Mar, press Tab, type twenty-four lakh fifty-seven thousand and press Return. The Table grows by a row and the chart picks up March by itself.
This is the mistake most monthly reports make: charting a plain range. Then March gets left out and someone stretches the range by hand every month. A Table removes that chore.
Now the dropdown. Select K1, then on the Data tab click Data Validation. Set Allow to List, Source to the region headers, dollar E dollar 1 to dollar H dollar 1, and click OK.
In K5, type equals INDEX, open bracket, dollar E 2 colon dollar H 2, comma. That's April's four regional figures. The columns are locked, the row is free to move down.
Then MATCH, open bracket, dollar K dollar 1, comma, dollar E dollar 1 colon dollar H dollar 1, comma, zero, and close both brackets. MATCH finds which column the chosen region is in. Press Return.
Select K5 to K16 and press Command D. Column K now shows North's sales for every month.

acts.h: Select K5:K16 and fill down with ⌘ + D

steps.say: In K2, build the title text: equals, quote, FY 2025-26 sales colon space, quote, ampersand K1 ampersand, quote, space region, quote. Press Return.

acts.h: Type ="FY 2025-26 sales: "&K1&" region" and press Return

steps.say: Select J4 to K16 and insert a clustered column chart: Recommended Charts, All Charts, Column, OK.
Link the title. Select the chart title; here I pick it from the Format tab's selection box. Type an equals sign, then the cell, K2 on this sheet, and press Return.
Now pick South from the dropdown in K1. The columns, the numbers in K5 to K16 and the title all switch to South.
Everything here works the same in Excel for Mac: Command T for a Table, Data Validation on the Data tab, and an equals sign in the formula bar to link a selected title.

acts.t:
Mac corner
⌘ T creates a Table
Data > Data Validation > List
Link a title: select it, type = in the formula bar, click the cell

steps.say: To recap: build charts on Tables so they grow, drive charts from helper cells with INDEX and MATCH, and link titles to cells.

acts.t:
Recap
• Tables make charts grow with new rows
• Dropdown + INDEX/MATCH helper = switchable chart
• Link the title to a cell

steps.say: Your challenge: add an All India option to the dropdown that shows the total of all four regions. The answer is on S11-10 Done.

acts.t:
Challenge
Add 'All India' in I1 with =SUM(E2:H2) down to I13
Extend the dropdown source to $E$1:$I$1
Answer: sheet S11-10 Done

lessons.title: Project: a Gantt chart for a project plan
lessons.mac:
Select separate ranges: hold ⌘ while dragging
Fill right ⌘ R · Fill down ⌘ D
Format pane: ⌘ 1 or Control-click > Format
Home > Conditional Formatting > New Rule > Use a formula

steps.say: This is the project: a ten-task ERP rollout plan for a Pune plant, shown two ways. A Gantt bar chart for presentations, and a week-by-week grid that colours itself from the dates, which is easier to keep up to date.

acts.h: Go to the sheet S11-11 Done

steps.say: You'll calculate durations, build a Gantt chart with the stacked bar method, and then a Gantt grid with conditional formatting. Practice sheet S11-11, recorded in Excel desktop.

acts.t:
In this project
• Durations from start and end dates
• Gantt chart: stacked bar method
• Gantt grid: conditional formatting method
Practice sheet: S11-11

steps.say: Here's the trick. A stacked bar has two parts: the start date, which we make invisible, and the number of days, which we show. Dates are numbers, so the invisible part pushes each bar to its start.

acts.t:
Stacked bar method
Series 1 = Start date (made invisible)
Series 2 = Days (the visible bar)
Then: reverse task order, start the axis on the project's first day

steps.say: Our plan has ten tasks with owner, start and end dates. B2 finds the project start with MIN.
In E5, type equals D5 minus C5 plus 1 and press Return. We add one because a task that starts and ends on the same day still takes a day.
Select E5 to E14 and press Command D.

acts.h: Select E5:E14 and fill down with ⌘ + D

steps.say: B3 shows the start date as a plain number, forty-six thousand one hundred eighteen. Excel stores every date as a count of days, which is why a date can be the length of a bar.
Select three ranges at once: task names, start dates and days. In the Name Box I type them separated by commas. With a mouse, hold Command while dragging each range.
Insert, Recommended Charts, All Charts, Bar, then choose Stacked Bar and click OK.
Excel draws a long Start bar and a short Days bar for each task. The Start part is just the gap before a task begins, so we'll hide it.
On the Format tab pick Series Start and click Format Selection. Under Fill, choose No fill. The tasks now float in the right places.
The first task is at the bottom. Pick Vertical Category Axis, click Format Selection, and tick Categories in reverse order. Now the plan reads from top to bottom.
Now the mistake everyone hits: the bars are squashed into a thin strip on the right. The date axis starts at zero, which is the year nineteen hundred.
Pick Horizontal Value Axis, click Format Selection, and in Minimum type forty-six thousand one hundred eighteen, the number from B3. The chart now starts on the first day of the project.
Click Chart Title, type ERP rollout, Gantt chart, and press Return. Then Add Chart Element, Legend, None.

acts.h: Type ERP rollout: Gantt chart and press Return

steps.say: Now method two, the grid. In H4, type equals dollar B dollar 2 and press Return. The first column is the week the project starts.
In I4, type equals H4 plus 7 and press Return. Each column is one week after the last.
Select I4 to S4 and press Command R to fill right. Twelve weeks, enough for the whole plan.
Select the grid, H5 to S14. On the Home tab click Conditional Formatting, New Rule, and choose Use a formula to determine which cells to format.

acts.h: Click Use a formula to determine which cells to format

steps.say: Type this rule: equals AND, open bracket, H dollar 4 is less than or equal to dollar D5, comma, H dollar 4 plus 6 is greater than or equal to dollar C5, close bracket. A week is coloured if it overlaps the task.

acts.h: Set Format values where this formula is true to =AND(H$4<=$D5,H$4+6>=$C5)

steps.say: Click Format, go to the Fill tab, choose a blue, and click OK twice. The grid fills in like a Gantt chart.
Notice where the dollars sit. H dollar 4 locks the row, so each column reads its own week. Dollar C5 and dollar D5 lock the columns, so each row reads its own task.

acts.t:
Why the dollars sit where they do
H$4: row locked, column moves → each column reads its own week
$C5, $D5: column locked, row moves → each row reads its own task
H$4+6: the week runs Monday to Sunday

steps.say: Plans slip. In D8, type equals C8 plus 34, so system configuration runs ten days longer. The bar stretches, the grid colours an extra week, and E8 shows thirty-five days.
On Excel for Mac, hold Command to select separate ranges, Command R fills right, Command 1 opens the Format pane, and conditional formatting is on the Home tab under New Rule.

acts.t:
Mac corner
Select separate ranges: hold ⌘ while dragging
Fill right ⌘ R · Fill down ⌘ D
Format pane: ⌘ 1 or Control-click > Format
Home > Conditional Formatting > New Rule > Use a formula

steps.say: To recap: a Gantt chart is a stacked bar with an invisible start, reversed tasks and an axis that starts on day one. The grid version needs one formula rule with mixed references.

acts.t:
Recap
• Stacked bar: hide Start, reverse categories, set axis Minimum
• Grid: one AND rule with mixed references
• Change a date and both views update

steps.say: Your challenge: add a rule that colours this week's column orange in row 4, using TODAY. The answer is on S11-11 Done.

acts.t:
Challenge
Highlight the current week in H4:S4 in orange
Hint: TODAY() between H$4 and H$4+7
Answer: sheet S11-11 Done
